$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.check.common.types. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-TYPEDTHROW-CATCH-REPORT-ONLY
arms.note: the catch-clause gate narrows to the report files, so a one-file `--fix` boxes a raw-string throw that a `catch (e: String)` in an unlinted sibling still catches — the wholesale-degrade twin of the S177 shape, found by T919's `string-catch` cell

arms.name: M-GATE-AD-EXCLUDE-BLIND
arms.note: an avoid-dynamic excludePaths file is reported as scanned

arms.name: M-EXPLICIT-TYPE-ORACLE-PARAMS
arms.find: for (index in 0...own.length) pushEdit(out, paramOracleEdit(s, fn, own[index], index));
arms.note: the oracle-assisted pass types no parameter

arms.name: M-EXPLICIT-TYPE-ORACLE-FIELDS
arms.note: the oracle-assisted pass types no field

arms.name: M-EXPLICIT-TYPE-STRUCTURAL-DECLINE
arms.note: a finding the structural fix leaves unfixed says nothing about why

arms.name: M-BAG-INITIALIZER
arms.note: a bag declaration whose initializer is a typed structure becomes a DynamicAccess its fields may not fit

arms.name: M-BAG-NULL-OUTER
arms.note: a Null<T> value is typed by its bare wrapper, so the bag becomes DynamicAccess<Null>, which names no type

arms.name: M-AVOIDDYN-COMPOSITE-SKIPPED
arms.find:
case Intersection(parts), Conditional(parts):
					for (p in parts) visit(p, inArgs);
arms.note: a Dynamic inside an intersection or a conditional-type branch goes unreported

arms.name: M-EXPLICIT-TYPE-MACRO-NO-PROOF
arms.note: no macro function's returns are proven, so `macro … return macro f($e)` stays an unfixed explicit-type finding although its type is Expr by construction

arms.name: M-EXPLICIT-TYPE-MACRO-NO-COMPANION
arms.note: a `return Context.error(…)` is no Dynamic companion, so getProjectVersion's catch arm blocks its Expr annotation

arms.name: M-EXPLICIT-TYPE-MACRO-ANY-RETURN
arms.note: every macro function is proven, so `return macro : Int` (a ComplexType) and `return null` get `:Expr`

arms.name: M-EXPLICIT-TYPE-MACRO-SHADOW
arms.note: a project's own `Context.error` counts as the Dynamic macro-API one, so a return of whatever it answers is taken for an Expr companion

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-OUTCOME-VALUE
arms.note: any value counts as a recorded outcome, so `threw = compute();` and `threw = other;` hide a handler that runs code

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-OUTCOME-DECL-KIND
arms.note: a parameter of the enclosing function counts as an outcome local

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-OUTCOME-FN-BOUND
arms.note: a read after the CLOSURE the try sits in counts as reading the outcome, though the closure runs whenever it is called

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-OUTCOME-EVERY-STMT
arms.find: if (hit == null || !readAfter(hit, tree, ancestors, fnAt, scan)) return false;
arms.replace:
if (hit == null || !readAfter(hit, tree, ancestors, fnAt, scan)) return false;
		break;
arms.note: only the FIRST statement of the body is checked, so a call or an unread second local after it rides along

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-OUTCOME-READ-KIND
arms.note: a WRITE of the local after the try counts as reading the outcome

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-OUTCOME-READ-BINDING
arms.note: a read of the same NAME bound to another declaration counts as reading the outcome

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-OUTCOME-READ-AFTER
arms.note: a read BEFORE the try counts as reading the outcome after it

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-OUTCOME-STMT-LIST
arms.note: a read in the other arm of the branch the try sits in counts, though it follows the try in the text and on no path

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-TEST-OUTCOME
arms.note: any receiver.method call in the body reads as recording a test outcome, though only the listed Assert calls do

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-OUTCOME-COUNTER
arms.note: an increment of a local read after the try (`failed++`) is not read as recording an outcome

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-BARE-VALUE
arms.note: a bare body that only yields a value (`null`, a constant) is read as a handler that does nothing, though it is the value the try produces

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-BARE-TAIL
arms.note: a side-effect-free bare body mid-list reads as the value the try produces, though the statements after it run on and nobody reads that value

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-BARE-DEFAULT-ARM
arms.note: a value body at the tail of a `default` arm is read as a swallow, though it is the value the arm yields like a `case` arm's

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-BARE-STMT-ONLY
arms.note: a catch of a try EXPRESSION with a bare body counts as a statement-context handler, though its body is the recovery value

arms.name: M-CATCH-DYNAMIC-LOGGING-NAME-IGNORED
arms.note: catch-dynamic recommends and arm (b) writes exception whatever naming.catchVarName says
